title: observability: token/kv enhanced logging, metrics, tracing + dashboards & alert tuning
author: Jordan Lee
description: Add token-level and KV-cache enhanced logging, tracing spans, and metric names + dashboards and alert tuning. Motivation: recent incidents (see SUP-7842) showed blind spots around KV cache misses and per-token cost attribution during low-latency tail events. This PR introduces: 1) new metrics (redwood.kv.cache_hits, redwood.kv.cache_misses, redwood.inference.token_cost_us, redwood.inference.token_latency_us) with dimensions: model, region, pool, request_route, quantization_profile; 2) structured logs for cache miss events (sampled at 1%) including request_id, model_version, prefix_length, and kv_key_shard; 3) additional tracing spans around KV lookup and KV load with durations; 4) Grafana dashboard updates that surface token-level cost/latency breakdowns and KV hit-rate heatmaps; 5) tuned alert thresholds to reduce noisy paging while still catching regressions (paging only for sustained >5% increase in token_cost_us p95 over baseline for 15m). The description below contains the checklist and rollout plan. Checklist: - [x] Add metrics and tags in runtime (runtime/kv_metrics.go, runtime/metrics_registry.go) - [x] Add structured logging and sampling (runtime/logging.go) - [x] Add tracing spans and propagate request_id (runtime/tracing.go) - [x] Update grafana dashboards (observability/dashboards/kv_token_cost.json) - [x] Add alert rule adjustments (observability/alerts/kv_cost_alerts.yaml) - [x] Add unit and integration tests for metrics emission - [x] Update docs (redwood-docs/observability/token-metrics.md) Migration notes: metric names are additive and backward compatible; dashboards reference new metrics but old panels are kept for 30 days. Rollout plan: staged rollout starting on Dedicated staging pools -> Canary in production for a single region -> Full rollout after 24h of no regressions. See linked Linear ENG-2431 for rollout schedule and ENG-2567 for alert tuning rationale.
commits_summary: Initial implementation: add KV cache hit/miss counters + token-level latency/cost metrics
Add structured logging for KV misses and sampling
Add tracing spans around kv_lookup and kv_load; propagate request_id
Grafana dashboard JSON + alert rule updates
Fix flaky test and adjust tag cardinality for metrics
Docs: observability token metrics and alerting guidance
review_comments: Ava Chen: Could we reduce tag cardinality for 'model_version' to avoid high-cardinality metrics? Consider adding 'model_family' instead of full git hash.
Jordan Lee (author): Good call - switched to model_family and added optional model_version as a span attribute only. Updated tests accordingly.
Diego Morales: The sampling rate for cache miss logs seems low (1%). Can we increase to 5% for regions with known flakiness?
Jordan Lee (author): Increased sampling to 5% behind a runtime flag OBS_KV_MISS_LOG_SAMPLE; default remains 1% for global control.
Samir Patel: Alert thresholds look reasonable but we should prevent duplicate alerts across regional stacks. Suggest dedup by alert_group label.
Jordan Lee (author): Added alert_group label and documented deduping in token-metrics.md.
Riley Kim: CI flake in tests/kv_metrics_test.go - appears due to timing expectations. Recommend replacing wall-clock sleeps with injected clock in tests.
Jordan Lee (author): Reworked tests to use test clock. CI green on re-run.
ci_checks: ci-pipeline: passed (re-run once due to transient e2e failure)
release_notes:
- Added token-level and KV-cache metrics for better cost/latency attribution.
- Structured sampled logs for KV cache misses.
- Tracing spans for KV lookup/load to surface serialization hotspots.
- Grafana dashboards updated with token-level cost/latency panels and KV hit-rate heatmaps.
- Alert thresholds tuned to reduce noisy paging; alerts deduped by alert_group label.
notes_for_oncall: If increased token_cost_us or token_latency_us alerts fire after rollout: 1) Check redwood.kv.cache_misses rate and cache_load latency spans. 2) Confirm rollout flags and sample rates (OBS_KV_MISS_LOG_SAMPLE) per region. 3) Use request_id from sampled logs to trace root cause. 4) Revert grafana alert changes via observability/alerts/kv_cost_alerts.yaml if necessary.
